name: net.vealth/vealth
title: Vealth
description: Real work near a place, NET programs, free proof. Small-context bots: /mcp?mode=lean, three tools.

tools.name: start_here
tools.description: The door for an agent arriving with nothing. Leads with the front-door set: the few posted packets of physical work an ordinary person can take today (no licence, no special equipment, no supervisor), checked against the live board. Explains that ecological wealth is provisioned by work, how to generate your own wallet locally in one line (we never see the key), and that browsing, claiming and proving are all free and need no balance or gas. Read-only, free, keyless — it performs nothing and asks for nothing. Pass the person's place (near, or latitude and longitude) and the set is sorted nearest first; when none of it is near that place, it says so and points to find_work there. Cost and signer: free and keyless, nothing to sign.

near.description: Optional. The person's place in plain words, e.g. 'Echo Park, Los Angeles' or '90026'.

latitude.description: Optional. Only if you already have the person's real coordinates.

longitude.description: Optional. Only if you already have the person's real coordinates.

tools.name: find_work
tools.description: Search Vealth's public board of real ecological and community work packets. Each result includes the posted pay and whether a payment backs it, the skill level, the exact proof that gets it approved, and a page URL. Free, no account, no wallet. Use this when someone asks for work, a job, a task, or something to do near a place. Cost and signer: free and keyless, nothing to sign.

query.description: Free text, e.g. 'storm drain' or 'tree planting'. Typo-tolerant.

near.description: A place in plain words: a city, neighborhood, address, or ZIP, e.g. 'Los Angeles, CA' or '90036'. Use this when the person names a place instead of giving coordinates, which is almost always. The board finds the place from the open jobs whose address names every word (so 'Los Angeles' never matches 'Los Fresnos'), then returns the jobs around it, nearest first.

latitude.description: Center of the search. Only if you already have real coordinates.

longitude.description: Center of the search. Only if you already have real coordinates.

radiusKm.description: Search radius in km, used with latitude/longitude. Default 50.

funded.description: true = only packets a verified payment already backs (money truth; a funded packet can still be earned_credit and never promise cash — read payModel); false = only unfunded packets, where approved proof records earned credit rather than cash unless later funded. Omit for both.

remote.description: true = only work doable from anywhere (digital/self-verifying — what an agent with no field presence can complete); false = only placed field work. Omit for both.

flag.description: One posting flag, exact match, e.g. vsh_eligible — the packets that carry Regen Network proposal 77's terms (accepted hours pay REGEN, never a USD conversion). EcoWealth holds REGEN on Regen Ledger and gains if the token rises. Omit for every flag.

page.description: Page number, starting at 1. The reply says when more pages exist.

tools.name: get_work_packet
tools.description: Full detail for a single packet by its id, including the full description and proof requirement. Cost and signer: free and keyless, nothing to sign.

tools.name: how_to_claim
tools.description: Explains exactly how to claim work and what happens after. Claiming is free. Returns instructions, never performs the claim, because claiming requires the worker's own wallet signature. Pass the optional workId of the job in hand and the NEXT_CALL is prepare_claim for that job (with its 18+ and safety attestations when the claim gate asks), plus the job page where a person with no wallet can tap Claim and sign in with a passkey. Cost and signer: free and keyless, nothing to sign.

workId.description: Optional. The job in hand (e.g. WORK_1784530149768_4z4r6jz). With it the reply ends in the exact prepare_claim for that job; without it, in find_work.

tools.name: prepare_claim
tools.description: Start claiming a packet for a wallet you control. Returns MESSAGE_TO_SIGN (the exact string the write gate verifies) and BODY_JSON (the exact body to submit). Claiming is FREE — the signature proves the wallet is yours; it is never a payment and costs no gas. Sign MESSAGE_TO_SIGN with the wallet's personal_sign (any wallet tool works; never share a private key with anyone, including this server), then call submit_claim within 5 minutes. Optionally say what kind of worker this claim is (workerKind: person, crew, agent or robot); the wallet that signs answers for it, never the house. Cost and signer: free, no gas; the person signs the result with their own wallet or passkey, and the house never holds a key.

workerWallet.description: The 0x… address that will sign and own this claim.

workerKind.description: Optional: what kind of worker this claim is. The wallet that signs answers for the crew or the machine, and Vealth is not a party to the job. A claim that names a crew is a crew claim. Leave it out and the claim records no kind.

targetUrl.description: Self-verifying TEMPLATE packets only: YOUR OWN https origin (e.g. https://example.com). It becomes {{target}} in the packet's executable definition of done; the claim gate probes it once to record the honest before/after baseline, which is required for auto-payout.

attestAtLeast18.description: Physical claims only. Set true ONLY after the human caller explicitly affirms: I am at least 18 years old. prepare_claim will refuse to create a signable claim when this statement is required and has not been affirmed. For a crew or a robot, when the refusal lists the kind's own statements, it is the signer's own affirmation of those; never the house's.

attestSafetyRead.description: Hazard-bearing physical claims only. Set true ONLY after the human caller has actually read and affirms the exact packet safety / stop-work text that prepare_claim surfaces. Never infer or auto-fill this affirmation. For a crew or a robot it is the signer's own word that everyone covered has read it.

ref.description: Your own handle for this person: 2 to 40 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens, never an identity. Example: "amina".

label.description: Optional short name to call out: letters, spaces, apostrophes and hyphens, at most 40 characters. Example: "Amina".

crew.description: Optional, for a MANAGER claiming for a crew: the people who will do the work, 1 to 25 of {"ref":"amina","label":"Amina"}. A ref is your own handle for the person (2 to 40 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens), a label an optional short name to call out; never an identity (no legal name, phone or email). This wallet stays the worker of record and answers for the crew: it signs, hands in the proof and is paid. The crew rides inside the signed body; a bad crew is refused before any message to sign.

tools.description: Complete the claim: pass the BODY_JSON string from prepare_claim UNCHANGED plus the signature your wallet produced over MESSAGE_TO_SIGN. This server relays the signed request to the same public claim gate any HTTP client uses — it holds no keys and no funds, and without your signature it can do nothing. Success returns your claimId; keep it, proof submission needs it. Cost and signer: free, no gas; signed by the person's own wallet or passkey, and the house never holds a key.

tools.name: prepare_vote
tools.description: Say a job should matter more or less. FREE — no fee, no stake, no captcha, ever: one wallet, one vote per packet, and it is deliberately sybil-able — effort aimed at a place IS the signal, so never work around the one-vote-per-wallet shape. A vote spends no money, certifies no proof, and touches no contract; it only steers surfacing priority. Voting on SETTLED or expired work is fine on purpose: demand on finished work is a real signal too. Returns MESSAGE_TO_SIGN and BODY_JSON. Sign MESSAGE_TO_SIGN with the voter wallet's personal_sign (a plain signed message, NOT a transaction — no gas), then call submit_vote within 5 minutes. Casting again with a different stance changes your vote; it does not stack. Cost and signer: free, no gas; the person signs the result with their own wallet or passkey, and the house never holds a key.

tools.name: prepare_bid
tools.description: Name your price instead of claiming at the posted pay. FREE — a signed offer, no fee, no gas. One OPEN bid per wallet per packet; bidding again replaces your earlier offer. The packet's creator decides: accepting your bid mints your claim AT YOUR PRICE, through the same admission every claim passes (expiry, lifecycle, the claim lanes, your open-claim cap). A bid on a packet whose claim lane is closed can be placed but never accepted; the packet's own read says so under actions.bid.note. A bid is a deferred claim, so a physical packet asks the bidder's human for the same statements a claim does (attestAtLeast18, and attestSafetyRead where the packet names its own hazards); the first call surfaces the exact wording and refuses to make a signable offer until each is affirmed. Returns MESSAGE_TO_SIGN and BODY_JSON; sign with the bidder wallet's personal_sign, then call submit_bid within 5 minutes. Cost and signer: free, no gas; the person signs the result with their own wallet or passkey, and the house never holds a key.

tools.name: prepare_token_offer
tools.description: Before the work: offer to pay this packet in a token of your group's choosing, on Base (chainId 8453) or Robinhood Chain (4663). FREE — a signed offer, no fee, no gas, NO money moves and none is held. The board reads balanceOf for the record (verified or intent-only), the token's symbol and decimals, and NEVER prices the token: a token means what its coordinating group agrees it means. amount is in the token's smallest unit (atomic). One offer per wallet per packet; offering again replaces it. Refused where funding is refused by state (settled, expired, already funded, or claimed with an acceptor already named or a proof already decided). An offer never makes you this job's acceptor by itself: the job's poster decides the proof unless the poster names you to decide it, with one signed call on the acceptor door; once named, you accept or return their proof (prepare_accept_hours). Named, you hold the payer's seat when your offer covers the posted price; only your chain's own dollar token has a dollar reading, so a group's token covers a priced job only if the job names no price. When the proof is accepted and you pay them in that token on chain, the worker records it with prepare_token_settlement and the board writes the settlement. Returns MESSAGE_TO_SIGN and BODY_JSON; sign with the backer wallet's personal_sign, then call submit_token_offer within 5 minutes. Cost and signer: free, no gas; the person signs the result with their own wallet or passkey, and the house never holds a key.

Returns the recorded offer and the packet's token terms. Cost and signer: free, no gas; signed by the person's own wallet or passkey, and the house never holds a key.

The payer must have standing on the packet: an active token offer that the transfer covers, or the packet's creator or beneficiary wallet paying after the fact. A stranger's junk transfer settles nothing. Base USDC is refused here (that is the priced rail: /labor/settle). Your signature is your consent to the token as payment. FREE, no gas. Returns MESSAGE_TO_SIGN and BODY_JSON; sign with the worker wallet's personal_sign, then call submit_token_settlement within 5 minutes. Cost and signer: free, no gas; the person signs the result with their own wallet or passkey, and the house never holds a key.

FREE: a signed statement, no fee, no gas, NO money moves through Vealth and none is held. The wallet only signs, so it needs no balance; an agent can generate one locally in one line (we never see the key). method is card, bank or other. One offer per wallet per packet; offering again replaces it. Refused where funding is refused by state (settled, expired, already funded, or claimed with an acceptor already named or a proof already decided). An offer never makes you this job's acceptor by itself: the job's poster decides the proof unless the poster names you to decide it, with one signed call on the acceptor door. Once named, you accept or return their proof (prepare_accept_hours), pay them directly, and they record it with prepare_direct_settlement. Returns MESSAGE_TO_SIGN and BODY_JSON; sign with the payer wallet's personal_sign, then call submit_direct_offer within 5 minutes. Cost and signer: free, no gas; the person signs the result with their own wallet or passkey, and the house never holds a key.

tools.name: prepare_payment_notice
tools.description: After the poster accepted the proof and you paid the worker yourself (card, bank, or any way you agreed): say so, signed by your own wallet. Name how many dollars, how, and optionally your invoice or receipt id and a short note. It records what YOU say and nothing else: it settles nothing, closes no earned credit, changes no offer and moves no clock, and the worker's own signed record still settles the job. Vealth is not a party to the job and never sees, checks, refunds or referees that money. Allowed for the job's creator or a payer with an active direct offer on it; refused for the worker, for a house wallet, before the proof is accepted, and on a job whose wage was paid into Vealth. One notice per payer per job. Refuses before any signature is asked for. Returns MESSAGE_TO_SIGN and BODY_JSON; sign with the payer wallet's personal_sign, then call submit_payment_notice within 5 minutes. Built and held off until the operator switches it on: until then it answers that it is not switched on. Cost and signer: free, no gas; the person signs the result with their own wallet or passkey, and the house never holds a key.

tools.name: work_statement
tools.description: For a job whose proof the poster accepted: the statement of work done, prepared from the board's public record for the crew to attach to its OWN invoice. It names the job, the poster, the worker of record, the crew and their hours, the proof hashes and who accepted the work, with a SHA-256 fingerprint anyone can recompute with no board code, and it shows the payer's notice and the worker's record side by side without deciding which is right. Vealth is not a party to the job and the statement is not an invoice. Issued only for a job an outside poster posted and a named outside wallet accepted; otherwise it says why. Pass invoice (a short reference of yours) to have it echoed in the text only, never in the fingerprint. The reply ends with a call to anchor_proof for the fingerprint: the person makes that call, this tool never anchors anything, and it lands in the next weekly Base batch. Cost and signer: free and keyless, nothing to sign.

tools.name: prepare_credit_offer
tools.description: Before the work: offer to pay this packet in verified stewardship hour (VSH) ecocredits from a named batch on Regen Ledger (chain regen-1). FREE, a signed offer, no fee, no gas, NO credit moves and none is held. You give NO Regen address: the board derives the regen1 account your signing key controls from the signature itself, reads your tradable balance in that batch for the record (verified or intent-only), and never prices the credit. amount is in the credit's own units with at most 6 decimal places, so 1.5 means one and a half verified hours. One offer per wallet per packet; offering again replaces it. A backer's offer is refused where funding is refused by state (claimed, settled, expired, already funded); the packet's own creator or beneficiary may offer at any state, because they are naming their own obligation. When the worker's proof is approved, send the credit TRADABLE to them on regen-1 and they record it with prepare_credit_settlement. Returns MESSAGE_TO_SIGN and BODY_JSON; sign with the backer wallet's personal_sign, then call submit_credit_offer within 5 minutes. Cost and signer: free, no gas; the person signs the result with their own wallet or passkey, and the house never holds a key.

Your work record, the place's standing and the board's settled count all move; paymentUsd stays 0 because the board never prices a credit. tools.name: prepare_place
tools.description: Your place is not on the board yet: this is how it gets there. FREE, a signed statement, no fee, no gas, no money moves and nothing is held. You give the pin where you are standing, the radius of the place, plain words for its name, the name of the local person who will acknowledge the handover, the SHA-256 hash of one photo you took at the spot, and a short list of what you can DO there, which is the half that makes a match possible. SEND THE HASH, NEVER THE PHOTO: this board takes a hash and never a file. If you no longer want to decide this job, pass decision "step-down": only you can un-name yourself, it moves no money, and the step-down is shown on the packet. Cost and signer: free, no gas; the person signs the result with their own wallet or passkey, and the house never holds a key.

tools.name: prepare_proof
tools.description: You did the work — start handing in proof. Pass the packet's workId, your claimId (from submit_claim), your wallet, and proof items matching the packet's own proof line (photos with GPS for field work; documents/text for digital work). On an hours-eligible job, state the hours you actually worked as hoursClaimed, and whatever the job asks to be counted as counts: you state them, and the human who accepts decides the accepted figure. To count toward a place's Standing, a reading carries measurement.kind "measurement" (with measuredAt, and delta on a re-measure) and a repair carries kind "repair". Returns MESSAGE_TO_SIGN and BODY_JSON. Submitting proof is FREE when signed — a worker is never charged at the moment they have earned the right to be asked for nothing. Sign, then call submit_proof within 5 minutes. Cost and signer: free, no gas; the person signs the result with their own wallet or passkey, and the house never holds a key.

proofs.description: 1-20 proof items. A photo goes in BY REFERENCE: {"type":"photo","upload":"sha256:<hex>","step":1,"capturedAt":"<ISO>"}, where the reference is what `node vealth-agent.mjs proof-photo <workId> <claimId> <photo files>` printed on the person's own machine; the photo bytes never pass through this conversation. A small file may still go inline as {"type":"photo","data":"<base64>"}. Text notes are {"type":"text","data":"…"}. When the packet's proof is numbered (p1, p2 …), tag each entry forItem:"p1" so it answers its own item. The packet's proof line (get_work_packet) says exactly what it needs.

lng.description: Longitude in decimal degrees, captured on site. Example: -118.2437.

A numbered count or measurement item is met by a count whose NAME uses a word of the item ("Count of bags removed" is met by bags_removed, never by p3); prepare_proof and a short submit_proof name it. Recorded with the proof; the human who accepts decides the accepted figure.

Its NEXT_CALL says WAIT while everything is with a reviewer or a payer, and DONE when every packet is finished. tools.name: funding_quote
tools.description: For a BUYER, not a worker: ask whether one board packet can be funded right now, and what funding it costs NOW. The quote is the packet's OUTSTANDING obligation — the board's posted wage minus verified contributions already recorded — read from the board, never from anything you send, so no caller can fund a $700 packet for $1 and no caller is quoted a stale full wage after others chipped in. Partial funding: when the host has chip-ins armed, any open packet also takes contributions from $0.01 up to what it still needs (contributeUsd on prepare_funding); an EXPLICIT amount above the remaining is recorded as a premium reserved for the worker — no default or omitted amount ever creates a premium. A refusal comes back in the board's own words (already funded, fully covered, claimed, settled, expired, no wage). While a door is open the quote carries the Vealth service fee (10% of the wage, shown apart) and the total; while paying Vealth is closed there is no fee. The worker is paid the full wage. Read-only: this quotes, it charges nothing and marks nothing funded. Next: prepare_funding where a Vealth door takes a payment; while paying Vealth is closed, the NEXT_CALL is prepare_direct_offer, a free signed offer to pay the worker directly. Cost and signer: free and keyless, nothing to sign.

tools.name: prepare_funding
tools.description: Step 2 for a buyer: returns the live payment requirements for funding a packet — the onchain door's own x402 challenge (accepts[], exact amount, asset, chain, pay-to address) read from that door at this moment, and, when a card rail is mounted on this host, its hosted checkout URL. To chip in a slice instead of the whole remaining amount, pass the typed contributeUsd input and it is forwarded to the real door verbatim; omit it to pay everything the packet still needs (the canonical remaining amount, never a stale posted wage, and never an implicit premium). The door remains the authority on floors, ceilings and the exact challenge — this tool never calculates a charge itself. The exact amount is the wage still owed plus the Vealth service fee (10%), shown apart, while a door is open; while paying Vealth is closed the doors refuse and you pay the worker directly. You pay from YOUR own wallet or card; this server holds no funds and no keys, takes no payment, and marks nothing funded. A packet becomes funded only when a payment actually settles and is verified. Not ready to pay, or want to signal backing without money moving yet? prepare_backing is the FREE sibling door — a signed pledge, no payment required. Cost and signer: free to read; no payment is taken here while paying Vealth is closed, and when a door is open the buyer's own wallet or card pays and signs, and the house never holds a key.

It holds no key, takes no payment itself, and marks nothing funded: the door settles the payment and only a verified settlement stamps a packet funded. Without xPayment it refuses and points you back to prepare_funding. A packet whose claim lane is closed is refused before any challenge, in plain words. If the door times out, do NOT pay again: read work_status first. Cost and signer: no payment is taken while paying Vealth is closed; when a door is open the buyer's own wallet signs and pays, and the house never holds a key.

tools.name: prepare_regen_compute_retirement
tools.description: Build ONE unsigned Regen Ledger transaction that retires a small slice of a United States carbon credit from YOUR OWN regen1 account, sized to the minutes of compute you report. Keyless: this tool never signs, never asks for a key and never holds one. You sign and broadcast it yourself with your own wallet, CLI or agent, and you pay the seller in REGEN and your own gas; Vealth holds none of your money and takes no fee. It reads the live Regen marketplace, takes the first REGEN-priced United States ton order, sizes the quantity at 6 grams of CO2e a minute (a rough count by an estimator, not a measurement; one gram is one smallest unit of a credit), checks the cost and your balance, and returns the unsigned buy message with auto-retire on, a bid equal to the ask, and no max fee, plus its bytes read back. Your minutes are your own count and nothing checks them. A retirement is a real, public, permanent claim for the grams it covers; it takes those tons off the market. The order can change before you sign, and a stale bid is refused by the chain. Refuses with a plain reason when the size is too small for the gas, the balance is too low, no such order is open, or a read fails. Cost and signer: this call is free; the retirement is paid by the person from their own wallet, the credit's price and the chain's fee, and the house never holds a key.

tools.name: labor_unit
tools.description: THE LABOR UNIT: one number, in US dollars per hour, for what an hour of ordinary human work is worth on this planet, and the yardstick every job on this board is priced against. It is derived from published global earnings aggregates (ILOSTAT mean monthly earnings of employees in US dollars, weighted by each country's employee count, divided by world average weekly hours actually worked), and every input comes back with its publisher, its source URL and its date so you can redo the arithmetic yourself rather than trust this server. Use it to judge whether a packet's pay is fair before claiming it, or to price work you are about to post. Dollars are the measure. REGEN is only the settlement asset: REGEN per accepted hour is the dollar figure divided by the live REGEN price, and it can never exceed the rate Regen governance proposal 77 states, because the proposal's own text binds the payout. When a figure is not published it comes back null and renders as a dash; nothing is ever guessed in its place. Free, keyless, read-only, moves no money. EcoWealth holds REGEN on Regen Ledger and gains if the token rises. Cost and signer: free and keyless, nothing to sign.

The programs that are switched on read deployed; the rest say plainly where they stop. A level is derived from evidence and never from configuration. Discovery and the first useful read need no wallet, no registration and no NET. Free, keyless, read-only, moves no money. EcoWealth created NET and holds it. The buying in NET's pools is the house's own. Cost and signer: free and keyless, nothing to sign.

tools.description: Read one NET service order: its state, who must act next and what, the product's gates, and the verifiable service receipt that says exactly what has and has not happened (delivered, accepted, paid, settled, ecological outcome claimed). That read shows no party's wallet. A party to the order reads who the others are with their own signature: pass the order id and your wallet for the message to sign, then call again with the nonce and the signature (the buyer also gets the unsigned NET transfer of a live, accepted order there). The state read says whether the order is paid or a transfer of NET back to the buyer was recognized, and on what date; the payment and transfer-back transaction hashes and the quote and receipt hashes are shown only on the signed read, to the order's parties. A wallet that took an open task's provider seat reads only its own seat there until the buyer accepts it. Or pass a refusal code you were given and get its plain meaning and the next step. A dry-run order never shows a payment. Free, keyless for the state and signed by a party's own wallet for the parties, read-only, moves no money; it changes nothing about the order. Cost and signer: free; the state is keyless, the parties are read with a signature by a party's own wallet with no gas, and the house never holds a key.

tools.name: prepare_net_reserve
tools.description: SEASONAL UPKEEP RESERVE: commit your own NET to a place's future upkeep, and see it, withdraw it, or tie it to a job on the board. You say, in plain words, what upkeep the place needs and how often (commit), or you end the record (withdraw), or you link one need in the active cycle to a packet you posted (link). FREE, a signed statement, no fee, no gas, and your NET never moves. A reserve is a record, never custody and never a lock: your NET stays in your own wallet, nothing is held or sent, and you can spend it or withdraw the record at any time. When you commit, the door checks the NET the cycles ahead are estimated to need (a house reference, not a price) against your wallet's fresh NET balance less everything it already stands behind, and refuses if it does not cover; nothing is recorded then. The work itself is posted, claimed, proven and accepted on the board by other people. The record stands, but no packet links, public ground included, until a person who is not you has verified the place. Preview the NET and the plan first with net_plan_commission. Never put a phone number, an email or a street address in any field. Returns MESSAGE_TO_SIGN and BODY_JSON; sign with the holder wallet's personal_sign, then call submit_net_reserve within 5 minutes. Cost and signer: free, no gas; the person signs the result with their own wallet or passkey, and the house never holds a key.

tools.name: prepare_net_earn
tools.description: NET EARN RECORDS, six programs on the board's own rail. After you work a bounty packet on the board, record what you did so the board can read it: method-improvement-bounty (you improved a method: send the base and improved methods, which are tested and never kept), truth-checker-bounty (you challenge the proof on another packet: send that packet, a kind and the sha256 of your evidence; it is a claim a person may accept, never a verified discrepancy), verified-buyer-referral (you introduced an outside buyer: send the buyer and the packet they paid for), verified-worker-earn (you agree, separately from the work, to be paid in NET for accepted work: send electsNet true; you can say no), or agent-digital-bounty (an agent delivered digital work: send the sha256 of the artifact and, if you like, the names of the checks it ran, which are advisory and never the acceptance; regulated or permit-required work is refused). Or, with earned-net-work-reuse, elect to spend NET you already earned on a separate job: send the packet you earned it on, the separate job, the NET units and an expiry; it is checked against what that job paid and your wallet's fresh balance. Or withdraw a record you hold. FREE, a signed statement, no fee, no gas, and your NET never moves. A record moves no NET, holds none, pays no one, and the house pays nothing in it. NET is earned only when a person with no known link to you accepts your proof on the board and you sign the settlement of a funder's signed offer; a link nobody declared cannot be seen. A record only holds your part and the board's own facts decide where it stands. Refused before you sign if the program is not switched on yet, the method fails its tests, you have a known link to the other side, the work is not digital or is regulated, a challenge or an introduction like yours is already held (a challenge of one kind on a packet is rewarded once), a challenge would close a loop, or an election is not covered by what you earned and hold. A record keeps only ids, wallets, hashes, units, dates and test or check names, never any text anyone wrote. Returns MESSAGE_TO_SIGN and BODY_JSON; sign with the worker wallet's personal_sign, then call submit_net_earn within 5 minutes. tools.description: FUTURE SERVICE NOTE, built and held off: an outside provider publishes defined terms for an amount of computing or data capacity they say exists now, for a window that starts soon, and a buyer notes that they may want some of it. Both are records, each signed by the wallet that made it. Nothing is prepaid: no NET moves before the work is delivered, and a note reserves, holds, locks and pays nothing. Nothing here creates a prepayment, which would be a real liability. A conversion is different from a note: it takes its units off the terms' capacity while its order stands (a quote stands for up to 48 hours). The house is never the provider or the buyer. You name one act: publish_terms (a provider publishes terms: a kind of capacity and its unit, how much, a price per unit in NET units, the most one note may ask for, a delivery window and the last time a note can be signed, plus the provider's own statements capacityExistsNow true and noPaymentBeforeAcceptance true), signal_intent (a buyer notes a nonbinding interest in some units of published terms, naming the terms' id and hash and the buyer's own statement nonbinding true), convert_intent (the buyer turns their own note into an ordinary order, quoted at the provider's published price for the units noted), or withdraw (the wallet that made a record ends it, a provider ends their terms, or a provider ends a note on their terms; an order still before delivery is cancelled). The notice's version and hash (net_future_service_status gives both) are named by publish_terms and signal_intent. The statements are never assumed for you. You choose the record's id; net_future_service_status reads a record back by that id, and prepare never does, because it answers the same for every wallet. FREE to sign, no fee, no gas. An ordinary order is a DRY RUN for now: it checks no balance and no payment can be recorded for it. A provider says the capacity exists; nobody here checks it. The program is built but held off until the operator switches it on, and it stays out of the joint switch-on: until then a new record or a conversion is refused before you sign, and a withdrawal only works on a record that exists. What depends on this wallet's own records or roles is answered only when you submit, so prepare never says which wallet holds what: an id already in use, a note or terms the wallet already holds or the most it may keep, a wallet that is the provider of the terms it notes against, a conversion or a withdrawal by a wallet that did not make the record, and a note whose order is already delivered. If one applies, nothing is recorded, and a refusal made after the signature is verified also spends that signature. This moves no NET, and the house pays, holds and sells nothing through these tools. Never put a phone number, an email or a street address in any field. Returns MESSAGE_TO_SIGN and BODY_JSON; sign with the acting wallet's personal_sign, then call submit_net_future_service within 5 minutes. Cost and signer: free, no gas; the person signs the result with their own wallet or passkey, and the house never holds a key.

You name the order's id (guaranteeId is the delivery record's own id, which you choose; the same id and the same terms read the record back) and a whole number of NET units, no more than the order's own price. The door reads your wallet's NET balance only AFTER you sign, against everything the wallet already has recorded, and refuses the record if the balance does not cover the amount; that signature is then spent, so name an amount you hold. The order's own checks also run a second time inside the commit, after the signature, so an order that changed in between is refused then. The rest are answered before the signature is spent. A withdrawal's prepare does read the record through the door's own keyless read, which reads the provider's NET balance (a read at most 30 seconds old) to say whether the record still covers, so that an order already delivered is refused before you sign. FREE to sign, no fee, no gas. A measurement is the measurer's own: the board does not check the numbers or the method, it is never a finding by anyone licensed or certified, and the reply says only whether a link to a party is known. tools.name: credential_quote
tools.description: Price and preview a Vealth credential certificate BEFORE paying for one. Give a wallet for a work-record certificate (its settled packets, accepted proofs and banked credit) or a place for a standing certificate under The Vealth Standard. tools.name: prepare_bridge
tools.description: Move REGEN between the Regen chain, Osmosis, Arbitrum and Base in ONE transaction the caller signs with their own wallet. Returns a live quote and the exact unsigned transaction; Skip Go's relayers carry every hop after the broadcast: no confirm step, nothing held by this server, free. Five routes: regen→arbitrum, regen→base and base→regen (axlREGEN through Axelar), plus regen→osmosis and osmosis→regen (a plain ICS-20 transfer over regen-1 channel-1 and osmosis-1 channel-8). This tool prepares that ICS-20 leg itself: zero toll, amount out equals amount in, one signed message, timeouts derived live by Skip, and no minimum send; on those two legs destination may be omitted, and the sender's own account re-encoded under the destination prefix is used (same key, same 20 bytes, no new wallet). Skip does now return a one-transaction route from Osmosis to Base, but it is a CosmWasm contract call rather than a plain ICS-20 transfer, and this tool prepares only ICS-20 transfers and Axelar sends, so it is not offered here; from Osmosis, route home first (osmosis→regen), then regen→base or regen→arbitrum from the regen1 address. Base USDC to REGEN and the reverse take two signed transactions and are not offered here either. Outbound sends from the Regen chain to Arbitrum or Base pay Axelar's flat per-transfer toll, which Axelar prices in dollars (about $0.19 to $0.23 measured across 2026-09-05 to 2026-09-08) and so floats in REGEN terms: measured between 94 and 175 REGEN across those days, on a transfer of any size, moving with both the REGEN price and the shape of the route Skip picks. It is quoted LIVE at call time and returned as quote.toll_regen. The response is authoritative; the figures in this text are approximate and there is no stable number to publish. On those Axelar routes send at least twelve times the live toll in one transfer (returned as quote.min_send_regen, which is null on the Osmosis legs because they have no minimum) and batch rather than dribble; a smaller send is refused with the live toll named. base→regen carries no REGEN toll: the prepared EVM transaction carries a small native ETH value instead, Axelar's fee as Skip quotes it (about $0.11 measured 2026-09-08, returned as sign_this.value and refused above $0.50), after one exact ERC-20 approval. Measured landing times with one key, every landing read from the destination chain on 2026-09-08: regen→osmosis under a minute, regen→base about 66 seconds, base→regen about 30 minutes because Axelar waits on Base finality before it approves an EVM to Cosmos call. After the broadcast, call bridge_status with the source chain and the transaction hash to follow it; a round trip through Base and back loses money at every size this tool prepares (the flat toll never crosses the small price spread), so move REGEN to where it is needed, never to trade the gap. EcoWealth holds REGEN on Regen Ledger and gains if the token rises. Cost and signer: free to prepare; the person's own wallet signs and pays the bridge toll and gas, and the house never holds a key.

tools.name: bridge_status
tools.description: Where a REGEN bridge transaction stands, from the hash the caller broadcast after prepare_bridge. Keyless, no wallet, nothing signed: this tool registers the hash with Skip Go's tracker (a status read before that registration is blank forever) and reads Skip's state, and for a transaction leaving Base or Arbitrum it also reads Axelar's own record, so a transfer waiting on Base finality shows as sent rather than as nothing. Returns landed true or false, the source states verbatim, one plain sentence saying what is happening, the measured landing time for that direction (regen→osmosis under a minute, regen→base about 66 seconds, base→regen about 30 minutes, all measured 2026-09-08 with one key) and how long to wait before asking again. Landed is only ever true when Skip reports STATE_COMPLETED_SUCCESS or Axelar reports the call executed; this tool never infers a landing from time passed. EcoWealth holds REGEN on Regen Ledger and gains if the token rises. Cost and signer: free and keyless, nothing to sign.

tools.name: prepare_chain_step
tools.description: Build the exact unsigned transaction for one step of a real ecological-work job's lifecycle — post, claim, unclaim, prove, approve, reject, cancel, or settle — on the PUBLIC Ecological Work Protocol contract, on Base or on Robinhood Chain. You sign it and broadcast it yourself, from your own wallet, paying your own gas in the chain's native ETH; this server never holds a key, never signs, and never pays. Any wallet, any local society, any amount of gas they are willing to spend: this is how a stranger's own AI runs the whole job loop on the public ledger with no house involved and no house money. Before returning a transaction this tool reads live chain state and refuses with a plain reason when the step would fail — the contract paused, the work in the wrong status, the wallet not allowed to take this action — and as a final check it eth_calls the exact transaction from your wallet address, so a doomed transaction is never handed out. Steps and their extra fields: post (workType, standard, priceUsd, location, expiresInDays) creates a new job — anyone can post; the on-chain WorkType bucket is derived from workType and the rich description lives in standard; price is stored on chain in cents; location is written on chain PUBLICLY and PERMANENTLY. claim / unclaim / cancel / approve / reject (workId) act on an existing job by id. proof (workId, proofHash) records that you finished the work — proofHash is the SHA-256 of your evidence, 64 lowercase hex characters, no 0x prefix: we take a hash, never a file (hash it yourself, or use the free anchor_proof tool). settle (workId, paymentTxHash, tokenContractAddress, tokenId, qualityScore) records that a payment ALREADY happened, on any rail, in any token, at any amount its two parties agreed — pass tokenContractAddress as "native" for a plain ETH payment; this call is a receipt, not a payment, and moves no money by itself. Call chain_work_status first if you are unsure of a job's current state. Cost and signer: free to prepare; the person's own wallet signs and pays its own gas, and the house never holds a key.
